title: Fewshot migration notes and quick heuristics
content:
Context and goal:
- Personal scratchpad: migrate a bunch of ad-hoc few-shot exemplars into a small, structured prompt library (jsonl + metadata) that works across model families.
- Primary constraints: minimize token count, preserve exemplar diversity, make order-robust, and surface a clear slot schema for downstream instrumentation (exemplar_id, task_label, difficulty).
- Why: existing ad-hoc sets are brittle across model upgrades (e.g., 13B -> 70B) and different quantized variants. We want a migration path and a checklist to validate parity.

Quicknotes / hypotheses:
- H1: Order-sensitivity reduces if exemplars are normalized (canonical punctuation, consistent casing).
- H2: Very short exemplars (<= 40 tokens) sometimes lose context necessary to scaffold complex reasoning — include 1 medium-length exemplar per set.
- H3: Rare entity exposure matters: if an exemplar contains rare named entities that appear in test, models hallucinate linking facts. Avoid exposing entity facts unless needed.
- H4: Stop-token leakage from example answers -> rely on explicit delimiters (###) instead of newlines alone.

Migration checklist (minimal):
- [ ] Convert each exemplar to structured record: id, prompt_in, expected_out, tags, difficulty, token_length.
- [ ] Normalize whitespace, punctuation (curly quotes -> straight), Unicode NFC.
- [ ] Run parity smoke tests: pass_rate on 200 seeds for current model and target model.
- [ ] Add negative exemplars where applicable (showing what NOT to do).
- [ ] Add 'edge-case' bucket with 10 adversarial inputs per task.
- [ ] Instrument exemplar usage in eval infra (which exemplar used for which query).

Example templates being migrated (working drafts) — use explicit delimiters and meta slots:
- TEMPLATE: classification-with-rationale
System: You are an assistant that classifies text into one of: [LEGAL, FINANCE, HEALTH, OTHER]. Provide a 1-2 sentence rationale.
EXEMPLARS:
---EX1---
Q: "Draft email about terminating a contract for nonpayment"
A: LEGAL
R: "mentions contract termination and nonpayment — falls under legal guidance."
---END---
---EX2---
Q: "Quarterly P&L summary with revenue drivers"
A: FINANCE
R: "financial report language, metrics referenced (revenue, margin)."
---END---
USAGE: append Q (user) and ask for Category + Rationale.
NOTES: rationale reduces ambiguity but increases token cost. Try switching to 1-token rationale label in low-budget runs.

- TEMPLATE: summarization-shotset (3-shot)
System: Summarize the following email into 2 bullets that an engineer needs to action. Keep bullets actionable and start with verb.
EX1:
Email: "FYI the feature branch failed CI because of missing dependency X. I fixed the tests locally but still hitting flakiness on mac. Can you look?"
Summary:
- Re-run CI and verify dependency X included in build image.
- Investigate mac flakiness with a local repro and report back.
EX2:
Email: "Customers reporting latency spikes after deploy. Graphs show magnitude only on region us-west2."
Summary:
- Check recent deploys in us-west2 and rollback if correlated.
- Run p95 latency profiling and attach logs for the timeline.
EX3: (medium length)
Email: "We need a short copy update on the pricing page to reflect new annual discount"
Summary:
- Update pricing copy to note annual discount.
- Coordinate with legal for new terms.

Failure cases observed during local migration testing:
- F1: exemplar-order flip: with models vA order [EX1, EX2, EX3] -> correct. vB -> better when EX3 placed first. Variation magnitude: 7–12% pass_rate delta.
- F2: truncation amplification: target model uses smaller token budget after quantization; last-shot gets truncated and output becomes generic. Mitigation: move medium-length exemplar earlier or swap for shorter mediums.
- F3: stop-phrase bleed: answers sometimes continue past explicit divider because model treats '---END---' as content. Use unique token like "<|EX_END|>" for library exports.
- F4: label leakage: when exemplar labels contain internal shorthand (ok, nit), model reproduces shorthand in production outputs causing UX issues. Standardize to full labels.

Adversarial examples to include in migration set:
- Inputs with nested instructions: "Summarize and then propose three follow-ups" -> many exemplars expect only summarize; model tries to do both.
- Inputs containing code fences and email headers -> model sometimes treats header lines as part of prompt. Use explicit instruction: "Ignore header lines starting with 'From:' or 'Date:'"
- Inputs with very uncommon tokens (unicode emoji sequences) cause tokenization mismatch across quantized variants. Mark these as skip-if-quantized.

Quick metrics snapshot (from smoke runs on baseline model, 200 samples each):
- classification-with-rationale: baseline pass 86%, migrated set 83% 
- summarization-shotset(3): baseline pass 79%, migrated set 74% 
- common failure: exemplar-order sensitivity accounted for ~6% of mismatch.
Notes: runs were noisy; need full A/B with logging enabled.

Instrumentation notes:
- Add exemplar_id header in request metadata (x-exemplar-id) so we can correlate exemplar -> downstream failure.
- Record token_usage_by_exemplar in eval traces to find high-cost exemplars.

Migration rollout plan (2-week sprint):
- Week 1: convert 6 highest-traffic templates, add instrumentation, run parity smoke.
- Week 2: run targeted A/B on 3 customers (internal sandbox) and collect failure traces; iterate on exemplar order and delimiters.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: should we include an explicit "difficulty" field as numeric (1–5) or categorical? Numeric makes sorting easy.
- Q2: what's canonical delimiter token to avoid model confusion? Proposal: <|EX_START|> and <|EX_END|>. Check escaping for all target models.
- Q3: policy on including negative exemplars (explicit 'bad' outputs). Might be confusing if model mimics bad examples — prefer explicit instruction "DO NOT" in negative examples.

Notes to self (short):
- Run full 1k-sample parity on infra with logging toggled next Monday.
- Talk to Maya about adding exemplar_id to the request schema (she owns telemetry).
- Add a short README in repo describing migration format: fields + delimiter rules.

Historical references / links I keep hitting:
- slack:#prompt-library thread (thread ts removed)
- GH PR: prompt-bank/pull/112 (migration prototype)
- jira: PR-7891 (migration epic)

End of scratchpad.
